references.text: Esau is the ancestor of the Edomites, and he was Jacob's brother, which explains why the Israelites are not to despise the Edomites—they are brothers.
This verse confirms that Esau is Edom and establishes the kinship between the Israelites and the Edomites.
Israel calls Edom their brother when they ask for permission to pass through their land, confirming the brotherhood mentioned in Deuteronomy.
God foretells that Abraham's descendants will be strangers in a land that is not theirs, pointing to Israel's stay in Egypt.
Jacob and his family go to Egypt, where they become strangers as mentioned in this verse.
The Israelites are reminded that they themselves were strangers in Egypt, and therefore should treat foreigners with respect.
Again, Israel is reminded of their experience as strangers in Egypt as the basis for how they should treat others.
Foreigners are to be treated as natives because the Israelites themselves were strangers in Egypt.
Obadiah warns Edom that they should not have stood by and watched when foreigners took Jacob's property, showing the complex relationship between these brother nations.
